title: Implementation Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

 

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

 

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

 

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

 

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

As an Implementation Lead, you're the bridge between customer needs and technical execution in enterprise deals. You translate complex requirements into practical, high-impact solutions, ensuring every proof of concept is accurate, scalable and positioned for success.

title: Intern AI Researcher: Anomaly Detection for Predictive Maintenance in Distributed Storage
descriptionHtml:
About Scality

Scality builds data infrastructure software for enterprise AI, cyber resilience, and sovereign control at multi-petabyte to exabyte scale. Its AI Data Infrastructure platform reduces operational burden through AI-powered autonomous operations while aligning the right storage media, performance, and protection to each workload through human-approved lifecycle policies. Built on CORE5 cyber resilience and open-code principles, Scality software delivers extreme performance, operational simplicity, and sustainable economics. The world's most demanding enterprises and government organizations depend on Scality to power AI initiatives, defend critical data, and build infrastructure that lasts for decades. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality is where AI remembers, learns, and thinks. F Follow us on LinkedIn. Visit www.scality.com and our blog.
Context & Motivation
A distributed storage cluster continuously emits telemetry at every level, from the platform and S3 service down to each server and disk. A failing disk, server or storage node leaves traces in these multivariate time series, from subtle shifts in a few metrics to system-wide disruption. Detecting and diagnosing these anomalies early is critical for:
  • Predictive maintenance: isolating or replacing a component before it impacts service
  • Faster diagnosis: pointing support engineers to the root cause, not just to an alert
  • Higher availability and durability of customer data
    • This internship is part of a joint research project between Scality and an INRIA research team. The project released SHAD (Scality High-dimensional Anomaly Detection), an open benchmark published at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). It contains 215 real 171-dimensional time series from Scality RING clusters, annotated for injected disk, server and storage-node failures. SHAD's baselines show the problem is far from solved. No detector handles every failure type, per-dimension attributions find root causes no better than chance, and off-the-shelf LLMs cannot interpret the anomalies. This internship builds on SHAD to close these gaps.
    More details on the project: scality.github.io/shad
    Your Mission
    As part of our R&D team and in close collaboration with INRIA researchers, you will develop AI models that detect, explain and interpret anomalies in storage-cluster telemetry. Your work will include: 1. State of the Art Review the literature and open-source projects on multivariate time series anomaly detection, root-cause attribution and LLM-based interpretation of time series. Also survey recent work on AI agents that automate research and experimentation. Starting points include SHAD and the TSB-AD benchmark. 2. Anomaly Detection & Diagnosis Models Design, train and benchmark models that improve on SHAD's baselines at each stage of the pipeline:
  • Detection that stays accurate across disk, server and storage-node failures (e.g., ensembles, hybrid models, time series foundation models)
  • Explanation: attributing each anomaly to the dimensions that actually cause it
  • Interpretation: turning detections into actionable diagnoses (failure type, criticality, affected component)
  • Early detection of progressive degradations, the core of predictive maintenance
    • 3. Fleets of AI Agents for Research Set up and manage fleets of AI agents that run your studies at scale:
  • Design agent workflows that launch experiments, run benchmarks and compare methods
  • Orchestrate and monitor many agents working in parallel
  • Build safeguards for rigor: experiment tracking, reproducibility, independent verification of results
  • Assess what agent-driven research changes in practice: speed, coverage, failure modes
    • 4. Evaluation & Validation Evaluate every model with rigorous, reproducible protocols. Use them to:
  • Measure each stage with SHAD's metrics (VUS-PR for detection, NDCG for explanation, a questionnaire for interpretation)
    Quantify performance per failure family and scenario
  • Identify which approaches are ready to transfer to production monitoring

    • Expected Outcomes & Valorization
    Depending on results, the work may be valorized through:
  • A scientific publication with the Scality and INRIA researchers
  • New methods and baselines contributed to the open-source SHAD benchmark
  • Reusable agent-based research workflows for the R&D team

    • Technical Stack
  • Python (primary language for modeling, experimentation and analysis)
  • PyTorch and scikit-learn (deep learning and classical models)
  • SHAD benchmark (github.com/scality/shad) and TSB-AD (github.com/TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD) for data, detectors and evaluation
  • LLM-based AI agents and their orchestration tooling

    • Candidate Profile
  • Final-year student in a Master's program or Engineering school (Bac+5), in machine learning, data science or computer science
  • Solid foundations in machine learning; experience with time series or anomaly detection is a strong plus
  • Strong interest in LLMs and AI agents, and curiosity for new ways of doing research
  • Good Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch
  • Rigorous and critical with experimental results, especially when agents produce them
  • Autonomous and curious, able to communicate results clearly in written and spoken English
  • Interest in distributed systems or storage is a plus, not a prerequisite

    • Work Environment
    You will join a fast-paced, lean AI R&D team. French and English is our primary working language. You will benefit from:
  • Mentorship from R&D engineers
  • Close collaboration with INRIA researchers working on time series anomaly detection
  • Access to real telemetry from Scality RING clusters and to the AI agent tooling the team uses for its studies
  • A high-trust environment where your findings will directly influence engineering decisions

    • Why Join Scality?
  • Work on a concrete research problem with real-world industrial impact
  • Build on a benchmark published at NeurIPS and contribute to open research
  • Practice a new way of doing research, with fleets of AI agents as research assistants
  • Be part of a team building infrastructure trusted by Fortune 500 companies
  • Potential to publish research or continue as a full-time engineer after the internship

title: Internship - UAV Robotics/Mechatronics (Drone Prototyping, Integration & Field Testing)
descriptionHtml:
Opening

WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP


Details

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: full-time (5 days/week)

Period: 6 months

Location: Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands


About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced on-board UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers that are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members have a background in different fields such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub located on the TU Delft campus in the faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.


Your role

If you’ve ever spent a weekend building a drone, tuning a flight controller, soldering a power harness, or figuring out why your FPV setup won’t arm, this internship is literally designed for you.

We’re looking for a hands-on builder who loves working with real hardware:

  • wiring sensors

  • mounting compute boards

  • setting up flight controllers

  • testing drones outdoors

  • fixing whatever breaks and making it better

If phrases like ArduPilot, PX4, Jetson, ESCs, power distribution, 3D printing, or FPV gear make you smile, you’re the kind of person we want.

This is not a “sit behind a desk” internship. You will be on the drones. You will be in the field. You will fly.


What you’ll do

  • Build and integrate hardware onto real drone platforms used in active R&D.

  • Work hands-on with flight controllers (ArduPilot) and compute boards (Jetson, Orange Pi).

  • Deploy and debug embedded perception software.

  • Solder, assemble, and prototype wiring, adapters, mounts, and housings.

  • 3D-print parts and quickly turn ideas into working physical prototypes.

  • Support and participate in drone flight tests (you’ll fly regularly).

  • Troubleshoot issues, iterate fast, and improve our hardware setups.

You’ll see your work fly, literally!


Who you are

  • You’ve built or flown drones / RC systems (any level counts).

  • You tinker with electronics, FPV, embedded software, or robotics.

  • You enjoy making physical things work.

  • You like fast iteration and getting your hands dirty.

  • Linux doesn’t scare you.

  • You are independent, curious, and resourceful.

We don’t care about grades, we care about what you’ve made.

Please include photos/links of:

  • your drone builds

  • FPV rigs

  • electronics projects

  • CAD/3D-printed parts

  • GitHub repos

  • anything that shows you build things

If you’ve ever crashed something, fixed it, and sent it back into the sky — you’ll fit right in.


Requirements

  • Enrolled in a relevant study (Aerospace, Robotics, Electrical, Mechatronics, Engineering etc.).

  • Linux basics.

  • Interest in UAVs, robotics, embedded systems, or autonomy.

  • English proficiency.

  • Organized and proactive.

Bonus:

driver’s license, drone pilot license, CAD, 3D printing, soldering, or flight experience.

What we offer

  • 1000 euro monthly compensation.

  • 10 vacation days during internship period.

  • (Really) flexible working hours and option to work from home 2 days per week.

  • Have a direct and significant influence on highly innovative products.

  • The opportunity to iterate quickly with tight feedback loops, close to the product. We are innovating, learning is to be expected.

  • Responsibility over the things you implement, you are the expert on what you build.

The application procedure

  • If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself; this can be a resume, website or other source, as long as we get a clear impression of your background and skills.

  • We’ll get back to you ASAP. If we feel you could be a fit for the position, we’ll invite you for an informal introduction so we can get to know you, and equally important, you can get to know us. After this, a technical focused interview could follow.

  • If at this point we feel you are the person we are looking for, we’ll discuss the specifics (starting date and period).

  • Welcome to the team!

title: Intervenant(e) en prévention des risques professionnels (IPRP)
descriptionHtml:
🐼 Pourquoi Prévenir

Prévenir est un nouveau Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail Interentreprises (SPSTI) en Île-de-France.

Notre ambition est de repenser la santé au travail pour améliorer l'impact sur la vie des salariés et l'expérience des professionnels de santé, en s'appuyant sur les moyens technologiques d'Alan.

Notre premier centre médical a ouvert ses portes au 117 Quai de Valmy (Paris 10ᵉ) et ce n'est que le début !

👉 Pour en savoir plus sur le quotidien chez Prévenir, c'est ici

💉 Le poste, concrètement

Nous recrutons un(e) IPRP (Intervenant(e) en Prévention des Risques Professionnels) pour renforcer l’équipe pluridisciplinaire de Prévenir, un SPSTI innovant qui accompagne environ 14 000 travailleurs en Île-de-France. Le poste est rattaché à notre centre (117 quai de Valmy, 75010 Paris) avec une activité mixte terrain (Actions en Milieu de Travail) et à distance (visio, webinaires).

Votre mission : contribuer à un objectif exclusif de prévention et de préservation de la santé et de la sécurité au travail, en accompagnant nos entreprises adhérentes sur l’évaluation, la hiérarchisation et la réduction des risques professionnels.

🧭 Parmi vos responsabilités

  • Réaliser des Actions en Milieu de Travail (AMT) : visites/observations en entreprise, études de postes, recueil d’informations (activité, effectifs, organisation, postes, procédés, produits, équipements, expositions, AT/MP, etc.).

  • Produire et mettre à jour des fiches d’entreprise et contribuer aux démarches d’évaluation des risques (DUERP, plans de prévention, registres SST, etc.).

  • Repérer, analyser et hiérarchiser les risques : physiques, chimiques, biologiques, ergonomiques, psychosociaux, organisationnels (TMS, chutes, bruit, vibrations, manutention, incendie/explosion, coactivité, risque routier…).

  • Formuler des recommandations de prévention en privilégiant la logique : supprimer → substituer → protections collectives → organisation.

  • Aider à construire et prioriser un plan d’actions réaliste (court/moyen terme) adapté aux moyens de l’entreprise, puis en suivre la mise en œuvre (indicateurs, amélioration continue).

  • Conduire des sensibilisations et formations (sécurité, thématiques prévention).

  • Participer aux CSE et contribuer à des enquêtes suite à accidents (selon besoins).

  • Contribuer aux actions collectives du SPSTI : campagnes de prévention, ateliers, webinaires, retours d’expérience.

  • Orienter vers des ressources externes si nécessaire (CARSAT/CRAMIF, INRS, ANACT/ARACT, inspection du travail, organismes de contrôle, consultants spécialisés), en lien avec le SPSTI.

Vous interviendrez dans une approche proactive : identification des entreprises à risque, propositions d’actions ciblées, et recherche d’impact mesurable.

👤 Le profil recherché

  • Enregistrement IPRP (DREETS) / certification par organisme agréé (uniquement si vous êtes à votre compte).

  • 3 à 7 ans d’expérience en prévention des risques professionnels (ou expérience équivalente fortement appréciée).

  • Domaines de compétence appréciés : ergonomie, psychologie du travail, hygiène industrielle, conseil en prévention/HSE.

  • Capacité à réaliser des fiches d’entreprise, évaluations des risques, études de postes (et éventuellement analyses/mesures selon votre périmètre).

  • Aisance dans le conseil et la restitution auprès d’employeurs et, selon les cas, des représentants du personnel.

  • À l’aise avec un fonctionnement hybride (terrain + distanciel) et les outils numériques.

  • Esprit d’équipe et capacité à travailler en coordination avec médecins du travail, IDEST, psychologues du travail, assistantes sociales, ergonomes, ASST.

  • Basé(e) en Île-de-France.

Vous vous retrouvez dans ces lignes ? Envoyez-nous votre candidature et nous échangerons avec plaisir.

  • Lieu : 117 quai de Valmy (Paris 10ᵉ) - dans un centre tout neuf, pensé pour la qualité de l'exercice médical

title: Java Developer (Regular to Senior) | Backend-focused Full Stack (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Become a Part of Accurids

Join us and help shape the future of pharmaceutical data!
At Accurids, we're building the data backbone behind life-science innovation. Our system identifies, links and standardizes critical enterprise data in compliance with global standards such as ISO IDMP. We help global life-science companies launch products faster, more safely and with better patient outcomes.
At Accurids, you'll join a collaborative, growth-driven environment where your work makes a real impact from day one.
As a member of our Product Development team, you will work with a high degree of autonomy while collaborating closely with backend and frontend engineers, QA, DevOps and product owners. You will work directly with cross-functional engineering stakeholders, and the features and fixes you deliver reach our customers. Our CTO is directly available to you as a mentor and technical sparring partner.

How you’ll make an impact:

  • Own features end-to-end, backend first: Design and build services, APIs (GraphQL and REST) and the data layer in modern Java and Spring Boot, then take the feature all the way into our React/TypeScript frontend. AI agents write most of the UI code, so your eye for good interfaces is what makes the difference.
  • Extend the platform: Build integrations with the systems our pharma customers rely on and extend the platform for customer-specific needs.
  • Bring AI into the product: Work on AI features inside the platform, from integrations with AI assistants to LLM-powered capabilities.
  • Amplify velocity with AI: Be part of our AI-native engineering culture. You use tools like Cursor, Claude or Gemini to speed up scaffolding, refactoring and test writing, while keeping architectural integrity, security and quality in view. As agents take on more of the routine coding, your role moves up a level. You direct them, help shape the architecture and own the quality of what ships.
  • Contribute to the architecture, hands-on: Help develop our modular architecture (Spring Modulith, platform and feature modules), optimize PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch queries and work with RDF semantic data structures.
  • Raise the bar on quality: Maintain solid test coverage (JUnit, Testcontainers, Playwright) and give thoughtful merge request reviews, including on AI-generated code.

What helps you succeed:

  • Backend experience: 3+ years building backend services in production. Solid knowledge of modern Java (21+) and Spring Boot (Spring Security, Spring Data JPA), PostgreSQL with Flyway and API design with REST and GraphQL. A Computer Science degree, Fachinformatiker training or strong hands-on experience as a career changer are all welcome.
  • Eye for good UI: You have a feel for good UI principles and are happy to own the frontend part of a feature. Experience with React and TypeScript is a plus.
  • Architectural thinking: You think in modules, boundaries and trade-offs, and you enjoy building what you design.
  • AI-native mindset: AI tools like Cursor, Claude and Gemini are part of your daily workflow. You treat AI as an output amplifier and combine curiosity with sound judgment about what ships.
  • Quality & delivery: Experience with testing at all levels (unit, integration, E2E) and GitLab CI/CD.
  • Location & work permit: You are based in Germany within a reasonable commuting distance to our Cologne office (NRW) and hold a valid German work permit.
  • Languages: Business-fluent English is required, and German skills are a strong plus.
  • Bonus: DevOps experience (Docker, Kubernetes, AWS), semantic web (RDF, SPARQL, Apache Jena), Elasticsearch, LLM or MCP integration, Material UI, or pharma/life-sciences domains (FHIR, IDMP).

Why you’ll love working here:

  • Grow your expertise: Deepen your specialization in semantic data platforms, AI features or platform architecture as we scale.
  • Epic Office & Hybrid Work: Work from our brand-new office in the KölnTurm, featuring breathtaking views over the city (even higher than the view from the Cologne Cathedral!). Enjoy flexible hybrid options. (Note: On-site presence in Cologne/NRW is required, and fully remote work is not offered.)
  • Community & Industry Events: Connect and grow your network through exclusive industry events hosted regularly right in our scenic office space.
  • Competitive Compensation: Fixed salary package of €60,000 to €100,000 per year, depending on experience, for a full-time, permanent position.
  • Work-Life Balance & Perks: 30 days of paid vacation, a personal learning budget, hardware of your choice (Mac, Linux, Windows), and your choice between a subsidized Urban Sports Club membership or a €50/month City Plus Card.
  • Empowered Culture: High trust, flat hierarchies and an environment where your decisions directly shape the product.

Not ticking every box?

We encourage you to apply anyway! We know great talent doesn't always follow a checklist, and we care more about your potential, curiosity and motivation to learn.
At Accurids, we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially encourage women and people from underrepresented backgrounds in tech, science and data to apply.

title: Junior Legal Counsel
descriptionHtml:
About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

  • Founded in 2014, profitable since 2017, unicorn since 2021

  • The number one issuer of new credit cards and loans in the UK

  • Backed by Balderton Capital and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan

  • Loved by customers & our team with top reviews on Glassdoor and Trustpilot

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Join us if you want to

  • Take ownership across a broad remit - you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Zable from day one

  • Work in small teams of exceptional people - who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

About the role

You'll join a small but ambitious Legal team with a broad remit, working with every part of the business, from Product and Engineering to Credit Risk, Marketing and People. Zable is an FCA-regulated lender operating in the UK, US and Mexico, so you'll get early exposure to regulated products and new markets. As Zable grows, this role is focused on commercial contracts, product and corporate work. You'll own matters end to end, explain legal issues clearly to non-lawyers, and weigh the legal position against what the business is trying to achieve.

What you'll be doing

  • Draft, review and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements. You'll lead on supplier and customer contracts, engagement letters and NDAs, and support on partnership and other strategic contracts as you build towards leading them

  • Manage our contract review process, including triaging incoming requests, providing templates and reviews, and managing the e-signature process (for example DocuSign) through to completion

  • Respond to day-to-day legal queries from the business and our counterparties

  • Drive process and knowledge management by building and maintaining document repositories, administering our contract management and AI tooling and helping us develop processes to support contract review and negotiation

  • Support on intellectual property matters and litigious matters as they arise

  • Take on company secretarial and governance work

  • Support corporate and transactional work, including KYC / due diligence requests and diligence reviews on corporate projects

  • Work closely with the rest of the Legal team to deliver timely, first-class legal support

How you’ll make an impact

  • You'll help drive the business forward by taking the initiative and embracing work beyond your comfort zone

  • You'll get to grips with new markets and financial products, bringing energy and curiosity to each new challenge


What we're looking for

  • NQ - 2PQE, qualified in England & Wales, or in another common law jurisdiction with relevant UK experience

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, including explaining legal issues to non-lawyers

  • Strong organisation: you can run multiple matters at once and prioritise them independently

  • Comfortable with pace and change, and keen to take ownership of a broad remit rather than a narrow specialism

Life at Zable

  • The opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

title: Junior Python Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We’re looking for a Junior Software Engineer to join our New Products & Geographies Engineering team in London. This team launches and scales new lending propositions in two directions: bringing Abound’s lending to customers in new countries and expanding our B2B offering for partners. We move quickly, exploring ideas through production-ready MVPs and iterating as products mature.

This is a hybrid role, with at least three days a week in our London office. It’s a great opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to grow quickly, work on real production systems, and learn how a high-growth fintech operates from the inside.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers who will support you through code reviews, pairing, and mentorship. We value engineers who are curious about the business and are keen to work with stakeholders to improve processes and customer experience.

Our technology stack

Python (including FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, procrastinate, SQLAlchemy and Uvicorn), Postgres, MySQL, Liquibase, Retool, Docker and AWS.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and maintain features in our backend services, which can span any part of the lending lifecycle – from finding and onboarding new customers, to helping underwriters assess affordability, through to paying out and collecting loans

  • Take part in the full software development lifecycle: contributing to designs, writing tests, reviewing code and helping with deployments

  • Write clean, well-tested Python, with guidance and feedback from senior engineers

  • Work with colleagues in Product and Design, as well as internal users, to understand requirements and turn them into working software

  • Work closely with our React frontend developers to build the APIs and backend logic their features rely on

  • Write and improve SQL queries against our Postgres databases

  • Help troubleshoot and resolve system issues that affect our customers

  • Gradually take ownership of parts of the platform as your experience grows

Who you are:

You’ll need:

  • 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience from a degree, bootcamp, internships or personal projects

  • Working knowledge of Python – you don’t need to be an expert, but you’re comfortable writing, testing and debugging code

  • An understanding of core programming concepts such as data structures, object-oriented design and unit testing

  • Familiarity with SQL, relational databases and Git

  • To be able to work from our London office at least three days a week

You’ll do well here if you:

  • Have a sharp eye for detail – in lending, small mistakes can have a real impact on customers

  • Learn quickly, take initiative and work methodically through problems, even in a large, evolving codebase

  • Communicate clearly, ask questions, take on feedback and work well in a team

  • Have a genuine interest in fintech and how financial products work

Ideally you'll also have:

  • Experience with async Python or frameworks such as FastAPI

  • Basic familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP or Azure) or Docker

  • Knowledge of lending products or open banking

How we work:

To be successful here, our culture needs to energies you. Here’s how we operate:

  • High bar and real ownership: We’re a high-performing team, and we hire people who raise the bar and take pride in great work. We own outcomes, not tasks.

  • Focus on impact: We measure success by what we deliver to customers. We prioritise carefully so our energy goes where it makes the biggest difference.

  • MVP and iteration culture: We ship fast, learn from real customers, and continuously improve our products and processes.

  • One team collaboration: We collaborate closely across engineering, product, operations and the wider business.

  • Thrive in change: Priorities evolve as we learn what works. We value people who use good judgement, adapt quickly, and stay focused on outcomes.

What we offer:

  • Equity – everyone owns a piece of the company

  • Hybrid working, with three days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days a year

  • A one-month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership through WellHub

  • A team wellness budget to be active together – set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

title: Lab Technician
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.


We’re looking for a detail-oriented Lab Technician to keep our Bristol labs running safely and reliably. You’ll support hardware engineers with testing, setup and equipment upkeep in a fast-paced AI hardware company.


Key responsibilities

  • Run routine tests and measurements across both Bristol labs, following established procedures

  • Set up, maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot lab equipment

  • Carry out basic soldering and small rework tasks as needed

  • Record results accurately and keep clear, traceable logs

  • Uphold health and safety procedures, including housekeeping, equipment safety checks and proactively reporting risks

  • Support audits, risk assessments and safe working practices, including for lone working

  • Help improve lab processes and SOPs

  • Keep both labs organised and stocked, and hand over clearly on the days you’re not in

Requirements

  • Experience in an electronics, hardware or lab environment

  • Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to documentation

  • Solid understanding of workplace health and safety, with a proactive approach to it

  • Able to work independently and as part of a team across two labs

  • Right to work in the UK

Desirable

  • Experience in or around data centres

  • Basic soldering and rework skills (IPC or similar training is a plus)

  • Knowledge of liquid cooling systems

  • A health and safety qualification (e.g. IOSH or NEBOSH)

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us!

 

Export controls

Our work involves technologies subject to UK, US and other international export control regulations. Certain roles may require additional eligibility checks to ensure compliance with applicable law. We'll be transparent about this throughout the hiring process.

title: Lead AI Security Engineer - Remote (UK Only)
descriptionHtml:
A platform you can believe in: Immersive One is the leading cyber resilience solution across the globe.

Build and scale a best in class platform alongside a team of the brightest minds in cybersecurity! At Immersive, we’re uniquely positioned to future-proof organizations against any cyber challenge. If that excites you, read on!

Immersive is the cyber proving ground for the AI enterprise. Through Immersive One, organizations can test whether people, AI-enabled workflows, cyber security teams, agents, and leaders can perform securely under realistic pressure, then turn that performance into evidence they can use to improve, benchmark, and report readiness.

Trusted by 30%+ of the Fortune 100 and ranked #1 in the Forrester Wave™ 2026, Immersive helps organizations prove AI can be adopted safely, teams can develop and defend at AI speed, leaders can lead through crisis, and AI agents can be validated before they are trusted in live workflows

https://www.immersivelabs.com/why-immersive-labs

We help the world’s biggest brands like Citi, Pfizer, Humana, and HSBC, protect their revenues and brand reputations.

Immersive was founded in 2017, from a cargo container in Bristol, UK we’ve grown to over 300 employees globally, announced funding of more than $180 million and been voted a Best place to work on multiple occasions!

https://www.immersivelabs.com/company/our-story

Lead AI Security Engineer - (Remote within UK)

Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next AI Security Engineer?

Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform, we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced, innovative, data-driven Cyber Security Engineer with a background in implementing security in AI products to join our Container 7 team as a Lead AI Security Engineer.

We’re looking for someone with a builder mindset who enjoys creating, improving, and scaling ways of working. You’ll have full ownership and accountability for your area, with real scope to shape the role and make it your own.

You’ll thrive in a small team with a broad remit, where there is plenty of opportunity to learn, develop, and grow alongside the business.

As a Lead AI Security Engineer, you will be a key player in our Container 7 team, shaping and influencing the rollout of our AI & Cyber security roadmap, simulating attack paths, demonstrating how to secure infrastructure and build security into your agents and AI landscape from day one - all while helping train our users to counter the latest threats.

You will be constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things AI security-related, from agentic security to the latest AI-driven attacks, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges for our customers.

This role would suit someone who is immersed in the AI security field and has strong insight and opinions on how our product roadmap should evolve to ensure our customers have the tools to learn how to build and deploy AI securely

You will design, build, and deliver practical and theoretical content to gamify AI security and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way.

If you have an extensive background in cyber security - in particular AppSec and cloud security - are experienced in the area of securing AI agents and securing AI-driven platforms, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats, we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market-leading platform, Immersive One, and our new AI Security product.

Your main responsibilities:

  • Utilising knowledge of offensive & defensive appsec and cloud security engagements to plan, write and deploy AI security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform.

  • Lead on the building of content around security vulnerabilities in AI and Large Language Model (LLM) deployments (e.g., prompt injection, data poisoning, model evasion). This could be multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification

  • Test AI Security labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected

  • Research vulnerabilities, tools, and offensive tactics and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users

  • Compile technical research into understandable, concise content for both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Work with the wider Product team on new projects and product innovations and how best to deploy them

Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas (we know it’s tough, but please try to avoid the confidence gap. You don’t have to match all the listed requirements exactly to be considered for this role):

  • Proven and extensive experience in application security, product security, or cloud security, with a strong focus on AI/ML or LLM technologies. It would be highly desirable if you are experienced in threat modeling for LLM and agent systems, agent permission design, Guardrails and output validation, evaluation and regression testing, model drift detection, and Drift prevention

  • Thought leader within AI Security - you’re someone who is constantly reading the latest whitepapers and thinking several sprints ahead as to what we should be building within our AI Security product roadmap.

  • Excellent communication skills to partner and build relationships with engineering and product colleagues outside of the core security team.

  • You’re a self-starter who is comfortable working with autonomy, takes initiative, and spots opportunities to add value.

  • You bring a hands-on approach, with a willingness to get stuck in and support across a broad range of priorities when needed.

  • Deep understanding of the AI threat landscape, including the OWASP Gen AI Security Project and MITRE ATLAS, as well as an understanding of adversarial machine learning techniques.

  • You possess strong attention to detail, have a logical approach to problem-solving, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.

  • Hold strong programming skills (e.g., Python) and familiarity with common AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain).

Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role:

  • Driven - We push the boundaries of innovation, acting swiftly to achieve ambitious outcomes. Our drive embodies a culture of ambition, where challenges are stepping stones to excellence.

  • Inclusive - Our strength lies in diversity, fostering a culture where every individual contributes to our collective strength. We champion open dialogue and empathy, ensuring a collaborative, inclusive workplace.

  • Customer Centric - We seek to develop deep relationships with our customers to help them achieve their business outcomes. title: Lead Product Engineer | 36labs
descriptionHtml:
Role: Lead Product Engineer

Company: 36 Labs

Location: London, on site four days a week. The office is on Baker Street and moves to Primrose Hill within a couple of months. London-based candidates only.

Job Type: Full-time

About 36 Labs

36 Labs is an applied AI research firm in London. It is working on a gap in today's models: they are weak at creative decisions and at explaining why a decision was made. The team's thesis is that if you solve creativity in LLMs, you have largely solved what captures human attention.

The product is a harness that sits over any frontier model, especially video generation models. It runs ideation, generation and distribution end to end. Content goes out to real audiences, and a data loop improves the harness over time.

The company is profitable and works with Sony, Warner and Universal through bespoke marketing partnerships. Marketing is the proof of concept, not the destination. A B2C offering is due very soon. V3 of the harness is being released internally, and it is a big scope of work.

The team is ten people, with four engineers working under a CTO who is still hands-on in the code. The seed round closes in the next couple of weeks. This is a new stage of growth, not a replacement hire.

What you are expected to do:

  • Own the upcoming B2C product end to end, from launch: an AI-native, customer-facing product where UX matters as much as the models behind it.

  • Lead product engineering: make product calls with the founders, set the bar for how things get shipped, and help shape the team as it grows.

  • Work across the stack on the harness and the products around it. The structure is flat, so engineers work on a bit of everything, depending on what is needed.

  • Help build and ship on top of V3 of the harness as it moves from internal release into wider use.

  • Take ownership of your pieces of work and move them forward with little hand-holding.

  • Work closely with the CTO and the other engineers, and explain your ideas back to the team.

What you need to succeed:

  • You have four or more years of hands-on engineering experience, including in the AI-native era.

  • You have owned something before, and you can point to it.

  • You take the lead. You see what needs doing and start, without waiting to be told.

  • You communicate well. You explain your thinking clearly and enjoy discussing it.

  • You live in London and are happy to be in the office four days a week.

  • You do not need visa sponsorship at this stage. The company cannot sponsor until about February next year. A visa that runs well past February is fine.

  • You work with Python, TypeScript and Postgres, and you know LLM and generative model APIs and open-weight models.

  • You build and run back-end systems in production, including deployment and operation. This is a strong plus.

  • You keep up with the latest stacks, models and engineering practices, and you have side projects beyond your degree or day job.

  • A degree in computer science, engineering, maths, stats or similar is a plus, and so is an MSc or PhD. The university matters little, and experience matters more.

  • Experience in applied generative media or creative companies, such as Fal, is a plus. What you have built matters more than who you built it for.

  • A notice period of one month is fine.

What you get:

  • A seed-stage company with a profitable track record since it began operating.

  • A strong CV line, and the chance to learn a lot quickly.

  • Clear room to grow into a more senior role. The long-term plan is for the CTO to move to strategy and the bigger picture.

  • Work on a problem few companies are tackling, with an extremely high ceiling.

  • Real clients from day one, including Sony, Warner and Universal.

  • A small, flat team of ten, with direct access to the CTO and the founders.

How to apply

Send your LinkedIn profile or CV to Alexander at the agency. We start with a short screening call. After that, the process runs as follows. First, a first-round interview with Benedict, head of operations, covering your projects, CV and motivation. Second, a technical interview with the CTO of about half an hour. Third, a take-home technical assessment. If the team cannot decide between candidates, there may be a final onsite round where you work on something in front of the team. Strong candidates may go straight to the CTO.

title: Location Data engineer
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly skilled Location Data Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will work with large-scale datasets generated by our products and turn raw data into meaningful signals, insights, and features.

You will work across the entire data lifecycle: building reliable pipelines, exploring and understanding complex datasets, developing features from them, and creating the tools and visualizations needed to understand their quality and impact.

This is a technical and product-oriented data role. You'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, and data teams to find what we can learn from our data and turn those learnings into production systems.

As a Data Engineer, your day-to-day will include:

  • Making Sense of Data

    • Explore large and complex datasets to understand user behavior and identify useful patterns and signals.

    • Transform raw data into reliable, well-defined features that can be used by our products and engineering teams.

    • Develop a deep understanding of our data: where it comes from, what it represents, its limitations, and how it can be combined to answer new questions.

  • Building Data Products

    • Design, build, and maintain pipelines that process large volumes of data efficiently and reliably.

    • Take ideas from exploration to production: prototype them on historical data, evaluate their quality, and build the pipelines needed to run them at scale.

    • Build datasets and features that can power product experiences, internal systems, analytics, and machine learning models.

    • Work with technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or similar tools depending on the problem at hand.

  • Exploring & Analyzing

    • Use data to investigate hypotheses, understand behaviors, and answer ambiguous questions.

    • Develop metrics and evaluation frameworks to understand whether the signals and features we build actually work.

    • Create analyses, dashboards, and visualizations that make complex datasets understandable and help the team make better decisions.

    • Build tooling that makes it easier to inspect individual examples, debug data pipelines, and understand why a system produces a particular result.

  • From Data to Intelligence

    • Work closely with engineers and product teams to identify opportunities where data can make our products smarter.

    • Use statistical methods, heuristics, experimentation, or machine learning depending on what is most appropriate for the problem.

    • Iterate on features and models based on real-world data and continuously improve their accuracy and reliability.

    • Help bridge the gap between exploratory data work and robust systems running in production.

  • Continuous Improvement

    • Improve the performance, reliability, and maintainability of our data infrastructure.

    • Monitor data quality and proactively investigate unexpected changes or anomalies.

    • Stay up to date with developments in data engineering, analytics, and machine learning, and bring relevant ideas and technologies into our stack.

    • Contribute to a culture of curiosity, craftsmanship, and learning.

Your Skills & Experience

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience working with data-intensive systems.

  • Very comfortable with SQL and manipulating large datasets.

  • Experience with one or more modern data technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or equivalent tools.

  • Strong analytical skills: you enjoy digging into data, testing hypotheses, and understanding why something behaves the way it does.

  • Ability to turn exploratory analysis into reliable, production-ready data pipelines and features.

  • Familiarity with data modeling, pipeline orchestration, and large-scale data processing.

  • Ability to communicate findings clearly through metrics, visualizations, dashboards, or other tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building data products or features directly used by consumer-facing products.

  • Experience working with high-volume event, behavioral, sensor, geospatial, or time-series data.

  • Familiarity with statistics, machine learning, or feature engineering.

  • Experience taking a data problem from an ambiguous question through exploration, prototyping, evaluation, and production.

  • Experience building internal tools or visualizations for exploring and debugging complex datasets.

Life at amo

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

We chose a location in central Paris, near Opéra (Metro lines 3, 8, 9 and RER A).

We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

  • Health care (100% coverage).

  • Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

  • Vacation days: 8–9 weeks (total) per year:

  • 5 weeks of paid time off;

  • 1–2 additional weeks (RTT, based on our company contract);

  • ~11 bank holidays.

We shut down entirely twice a year, two weeks in summer and one week in winter, to allow everyone to truly recharge and avoid prolonged slowdowns. These pauses are part of your total vacation time, giving everyone a real chance to unplug and recharge. No Slack, no email, no FOMO.

title: Marketing - First Hire (m/f/d), German Speaking
descriptionHtml:
About The Company

At NaroIQ, we believe the fund industry is undergoing a structural shift: investors are more cost-conscious and transparency-driven than ever, and ETFs are a natural outcome of this shift.

Yet many capital management companies (ManCos) excel at running traditional mutual funds - but struggle to enter the ETF market. Launching and operating ETFs adds a new layer of complexity: new partners, interfaces, processes, and systems that most existing setups weren't built for.

NaroIQ gives ManCos a fast, reliable path into the ETF market. We provide the digital ETF infrastructure that reduces operational complexity, so ManCos can launch and run ETFs at scale and compete effectively, helping broaden access to the market beyond dominant, US-based providers.

We are remote-first, with in-person collaboration opportunities. We work with international clients and have raised over $10m from top-tier investors and operators across finance and technology.

The Role and What Makes It Special

You own the two functions that decide how the outside world experiences NaroIQ: How we are perceived in the market, and who we manage to attract to build it. Marketing and Employer Branding sit together in one role at NaroIQ because the same narrative - sharp, technical, high quality - has to land with senior executives and journalists as well as with the engineers, operators and commercial talent we want to hire next.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role. You will not manage a team of specialists who do the work - you'll do the work: drafting the LinkedIn post, creating our brand strategy, building relationships with journalists, organizing events, designing an employer brand. And you'll build the systems that let NaroIQ scale this without losing sharpness.

There is no marketing playbook to inherit and nobody above you in the function. You set the priorities, decide what not to do, and carry the call. That takes unusual self-drive - the kind where nobody has to ask you for a status update, and where an unclear brief is something you resolve rather than escalate.

You report to the CEO (Chris) and work in tight loops with Growth, Product and the leadership team. Over time, you have the opportunity to grow the function around you.

Tasks

What You'll Do

PR & Events

  • Run PR campaigns end-to-end, directly and with external PR partners, to build durable credibility and secure consistent placements in tier-1 outlets (Handelsblatt, Bloomberg, FT) and the FinTech and asset-management publications that matter
  • Build and maintain a working network of journalists and editors; develop narratives that sharpen NaroIQ's positioning
  • Plan and coordinate events and speaking slots (e.g. Money20/20, FinTech and asset-management conferences, exclusive industry roundtables)

Content & Brand

  • Build a scalable content and thought-leadership engine that actively supports sales enablement and pipeline progression
  • Grow NaroIQ's organic LinkedIn presence at the company and founder level. A steady cadence of substantive posts, not noise.
  • Build and maintain a consistent brand identity across every surface: website, pitch deck, one-pagers, careers page, sales collateral
  • Create a brand that sticks with our audience: You decide how we are perceived in the market and what the NaroIQ storyline should look like

Demand Generation & Sales Alignment

  • Develop the materials that prepare and accelerate enterprise conversations: one-pagers, decks, whitepapers, case studies
  • Build and run inbound growth motions: SEO, AI search optimization, and targeted growth experiments
  • Close the loop with Sales: instrument what's working, kill what isn't, feed campaign learnings back into product and positioning

Employer Branding

  • Build NaroIQ's employer brand into a real asset: a careers narrative that pulls senior talent in, a candidate experience that earns referrals
  • Position NaroIQ as one of the most attractive places to work in European FinTech; through content, events, founder presence, and glimpses into the lived experience of the team

Requirements

What We're Looking For

(You don't need to know it all - but you should be ready to dive in, learn fast, and take initiative.)

  • Experience in B2B marketing: Ideally in financial services or at an AI / enterprise startup
  • You can create a brand, not just run one: you've built positioning and narrative for a product or category, ideally while the product was still moving
  • Creative and strong at storytelling: You can draft an explanatory case study, a press pitch that lands, and a job description that pulls. Without slipping into FinTech buzzwords
  • Extroverted and a strong communicator: You build real relationships with journalists, candidates and event coordinators
  • Existing PR network or demonstrable track record in media work is a big plus
  • Data-driven: You think in KPIs and processes, and use them to make the work sharper
  • Experimental: You actively try new channels and formats, like AI search, new social formats, distribution plays
  • You treat candidates as an audience: you can write a role description that makes people apply, shape how NaroIQ shows up to talent, and equip hiring managers with a story worth telling
  • A taste-led approach to brand: you can hold a consistent visual and verbal system across surfaces and push back on output that breaks it
  • Structured and genuinely self-directed: you're comfortable operating with ambiguity, high ownership and no cover in a small, fast-moving team
  • Fluent in English and German, written and spoken

Nice to have: existing relationships with FinTech or asset-management journalists; experience building a careers brand from scratch; familiarity with growth tooling (SEO, attribution, growth-hacking stacks).

Why NaroIQ

We're building something ambitious - and we believe the only way to do that is with a team that's low-ego, high-impact, and genuinely excited about what they're doing.

Here's what we care about:

🔑 High Ownership
We trust you to take full responsibility for your work. That means freedom and also being the person others rely on when things get real.

🚫 No Bullshit, No Ego
We're too small for politics, posturing or competing agendas. We care about doing the right thing, not being right.

🧘‍♂️ Flexibility
Exceptional work doesn't require relocation or fixed office hours. Have dinner with your family. Get that dog. Move to the Alps. We're remote-first and trust people to manage their own time.

🧳 Sometimes We Leave the House
We do make time for real-life moments, like quarterly offsites or in-person team sessions, to solve stuff together or just hang out.

🦸🏻‍♀️ Hire for Spikes
We don't expect you to be good at everything. We care about your superpower. We're building a team of nerds who are world-class in wildly different areas.

🛠 Default to Rethink
We don't accept "that's just how it is." We dig deep, think from scratch and always believe there's a better way. First Principles isn't a buzzword for us.

💅🏼 Give Yourself a Little Treat
We offer benefits via hrmony, so you can spend up to €50/month on the little things that bring you joy: Urban Sports, DAZN, Mediamarkt, Thalia, whatever suits you.

🤓 Your Learning Curve is Our Investment
Everyone at NaroIQ gets €1,000 per year for courses, books, coaching, or whatever helps them grow.

Dann ein 45-minütiger Termin mit einer praktischen Aufgabe aus dem echten Alltag – zum Beispiel ein LinkedIn-Post zu einem regulatorischen Thema –, damit du siehst, was dich erwartet, und wir sehen, wie du arbeitest. title: Mechanical Engineer - Antenna Positioning & Ground Equipment
descriptionHtml:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

The challenge

We build the ground equipment that keeps our interceptor drones connected, and it must be set up fast by a single operator in harsh field conditions. Mechanics decide whether antennas stay on target and whether electronics survive transport, weather and rough handling. You will go from CAD to prototypes to field tests, working hands-on with RF, electrical and operations colleagues.

Missions

  • Design an antenna positioning system: drive train, cable management, stiffness and wind resistance.

  • Design rugged enclosures for radio modules and electronics: sealing, thermal management, mounting.

  • Evaluate off-the-shelf solutions: compare commercial positioners and mounts against our needs and support buy-vs-build decisions.

  • Build modularity into the ground equipment: common interfaces, quick set-up, easy maintenance.

  • Take parts from prototype to production: 3D printing to machined parts, drawings, mechanical BOM, assembly instructions.

  • Support field trials and deployments: set-up, feedback from operators, design fixes.

Required skills

  • Engineering degree in mechanical or mechatronics engineering, with experience designing electromechanical products.

  • Solid mechanism design fundamentals: tolerancing, gears and reductions, bearings, structural and wind-load calculations.

  • CAD (Fusion 360 or SolidWorks), design for manufacturing and assembly, rapid prototyping (3D printing, CNC).

  • Rugged outdoor design (sealing, thermal, vibration); experience with antenna trackers, gimbals, drones or defense equipment is a plus.

  • Working knowledge of motion systems (motors, encoders, drives) to collaborate with electrical and software teams.

  • Hands-on and autonomous, available for frequent field trials and travel.

title: MI Analyst
descriptionHtml:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

The role

As our MI Analyst, you will tell our Contact Centre leaders what the data means and what to do about it, then build the tools that deliver it at scale. You will sit in the Workforce Planning team, working across all teams who deal with customer contacts and report to the Head of Workforce Planning. Each day, week and month we publish reporting on agent productivity, operational performance and business review data across multiple teams and two sites. The job is to go beyond filling in the numbers and answer the "so what":

  • What are our most immediate opportunities?

  • What do we do about them with operational leaders?

  • Where are we losing efficiency?

  • Where could the same hours deliver more?

You will also use AI to do this faster than any manual process could. We run Claude connected to our BI data lake, so the right person can pull data, build reports and automate repeatable work themselves, without waiting in a queue. We want someone who sees that and immediately starts asking what they can automate.

What you will do

Find the insight

  • Turn Contact Centre data into clear findings and recommendations, and tell leaders what to do, not just what happened.

  • Spot where we are losing efficiency or capacity, size each opportunity, and prioritise the ones worth acting on.

  • Add commentary to the reports you publish, so readers see the story behind the numbers.

  • Own our understanding of contact drivers: explain why customers contact us, how that is changing, and what we could do to reduce it or handle it better.

Build with AI, at scale

  • Use Claude and our BI data lake to pull data, build reports and automate manual collation.

  • Replace repeatable, manual reporting with automated, reliable processes, so your time goes on analysis.

  • Bring us ideas for what to automate next, and show the time and capacity you save.

  • Document what you build so others in the team can run and maintain it when required.

Run the reporting cadence

  • Deliver daily, weekly and monthly reporting on agent productivity, utilisation and key service metrics across phone, email, chat and messaging.

  • Prepare the data for our daily, weekly and monthly business reviews (WBR and MBR).

  • Keep stakeholders updated on what you are working on and when it will land, without being asked.

Own accuracy

  • Validate every output before you share it. You are the last line of quality control on your own work.

  • Check sources and definitions rather than trusting historical reports, and flag anything that looks wrong before others find it.

  • Cross check your reports against the WBR and other sources, so mismatches show up before stakeholders spot them.

Be our Contact Centre data partner to BI

  • Act as the Contact Centre data partner to our BI teams, and the link between them and our operational leaders.

  • Help validate data models, dashboards and metrics against what is really happening on the floor.

  • Spot data issues early, raise them with BI with clear examples, and see them through to a fix.

  • Turn operational questions into clear requirements for BI, and help test what they build before it goes live.

  • Keep metric definitions consistent across Zendesk, Talkdesk, Calabrio and Looker.

Work with the business

  • Understand what team leaders and managers need from the data, and challenge whether our metrics are the right ones.

  • Help define and evolve Contact Centre KPIs as the business grows.

  • Support ad hoc analysis and reporting on test and learn initiatives, and on BPO partner performance.

What we are looking for

We want someone who has already worked with data in a busy operation and wants to do much more with it. If you are curious, thorough and keen to build, we want to hear from you.

You will need

  • Real curiosity about data. You ask why a number moved, not just what it is.

  • The ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation that a non-technical leader can act on.

  • Strong attention to detail, and the habit of sense checking your own work before anyone else sees it.

  • Experience as an analyst, with a real understanding of the data you work with: where it comes from, how it is built, and what it can and cannot tell you.

  • Hands on experience using AI tools such as Claude to analyse data or build things, or a strong track record of picking up new tools fast.

  • Strong written and spoken communication, including working with BI teams to validate data and proactively updating stakeholders on progress and delays.

  • A drive to take ownership, without being prompted, of the reports and processes you run.

  • The ability to manage daily and weekly deadlines in a fast moving operation.

It would be great if you have

  • Experience in a Contact Centre or operations environment, and working knowledge of how AHT, occupancy, SLA and productivity are measured and what moves them.

  • Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Looker Studio or similar BI tools.

  • Experience with Zendesk, Talkdesk or Calabrio data.

  • Examples of something you automated or built that saved real time.

Why join us

  • Claude connected to our BI data lake, so you can build with real, live data from day one.

  • Your work is used every morning by operational leaders to run the day and directly impacts business performance.

  • Room to move from running reports to owning our Ops reporting automation.

  • A small team where good ideas get picked up and shipped.

Benefits

We've got your back, in life's biggest moments and the everyday ones too.

  • £34,000 per annum

  • Equity scheme - we all share in Motorway’s success

  • 33 days holiday (inclusive of bank holidays)

  • Sea-front office with bi-weekly massages and free snacks

  • Private medical insurance via BUPA

  • Life assurance

  • Pension scheme (we contribute 5%)

  • Enhanced family leave (e.g. 26 weeks full pay for maternity or adoption)

  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme

  • EV leasing scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Nursery salary sacrifice scheme

  • 1 paid volunteering day a year

Equal Opportunities Statement

Motorway is committed to equality of opportunity for all employees. We work to provide a supportive and inclusive environment where all individuals can maximise their full potential. We believe our workforce should reflect a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives and experiences. Our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion is evident through our constant focus on recruiting, developing and advancing individuals based on their skills and talents.

We welcome applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

title: ML Data & Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for an ML Data & Platform Engineer to own the infrastructure that powers our speech AI models: the pipelines that source and prepare training data, and the platform that trains, evaluates, and serves them in production. Speech AI has a data problem most ML teams don't, and you'll be at the centre of solving it, working as part of our ML team to remove friction across the entire lifecycle and get better models into production faster.

This is a broad, cross-functional role suited to someone who enjoys working across the full stack: data infrastructure, distributed systems, and production ML, and who takes ownership of problems end to end rather than waiting to be told what to fix.

What you'll do

  • Designing, building, and maintaining scalable data pipelines for ingesting, transforming, validating, and storing large datasets used to train our models
  • Developing and maintaining web scraping and data acquisition solutions to keep training datasets fresh, high-quality, and available at scale
  • Building and operating the infrastructure that lets the ML team deploy and evaluate new models quickly, and that serves models efficiently and reliably in production
  • Optimising infrastructure for both iteration speed and production reliability, including GPU utilisation, job scheduling, and training efficiency
  • Implementing observability (monitoring, logging, alerting) across data pipelines and ML systems to catch issues early and keep things running smoothly
  • Troubleshooting complex issues across distributed systems, spanning data infrastructure, training, and inference
  • Continuously improving our data and MLOps practices, and helping shape the roadmap for how our platform evolves as we scale

What you'll need

  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with a solid backend or data engineering foundation
  • Hands-on experience with containerisation and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), and working with a major cloud provider
  • Experience building data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes at scale, including web scraping or automated data collection
  • A solid understanding of the ML lifecycle, from data through to model training, evaluation, and serving
  • Experience with data quality practices (validation, cleaning, normalisation) and/or production-grade observability
  • Ability to design resilient, scalable architectures, and comfort operating and troubleshooting distributed systems
  • MLOps experience, for example model serving, experiment tracking, GPU/distributed training optimisation, or reproducible ML workflows
  • A self-starter mentality: comfortable identifying problems and driving fixes without needing detailed direction

We encourage you to apply even if you do not feel you match all of the requirements exactly. The list of requirements is intended to show the kinds of experience and qualities we’re looking for, but it is not exhaustive. If you are interested in the role, the team, and our mission, we would love to consider your application. We are always open to conversations and look forward to hearing from you.

Who we are:

Speechmatics is the leading expert in Speech Intelligence, and uses AI and Machine Learning to unlock business value in human speech worldwide. We work with an amazing mix of global companies, and our technology can integrate into our customers stack irrespective of their industry or use case – making it the go-to solution to harness useful information from speech.

Joining us means working with some of the smartest minds around the world, focused on cutting-edge projects and deploying the latest techniques to disrupt the market. We believe in putting people first; we’ll do all we can to help you develop your skills and give you the tools you need to thrive. Our Focus Fridays give you an undisturbed day of focus, offset with Together Tuesdays when we have our team meetings, so you've always got the right balance.

We have structured a hybrid approach that includes 2-3 designated office days each week. This arrangement ensures that while we embrace the advantages of remote work, we also maintain the vital connection and synergy that only in-person interactions can foster.

This is only the beginning; we’re looking for amazing people like you to continue our journey…

What we can offer you:

No matter what stage of your career you’re at - from paid internships and first-job opportunities through to management and senior positions - we’ll support you with the training and development needed to reach your career aspirations with us. There really is no shortage of opportunities here for you to get involved and collaborate with those around you to deliver your best work.

We offer incredibly flexible working, regular company lunches, and birthday celebrations. But that’s not all. We’ve spoken to our teams to find out what they want. From Private Medical, and Dental for you and your family, through to global working opportunities, a generous holiday allowance and pension/401K matching, we want to make sure our employees and their families are looked after. Every employee will receive a working from home allowance for tech or home office equipment (on top of your choice of laptop and accessories of course). Our approach to parental leave is designed to support employees globally. While this varies by geo, we have support in place for parents (including adoption assistance and reproductive health services) to ensure they have the time and financial resources needed to care for their growing families.

At Speechmatics, our mission is simple: Understand Every Voice out there. 

That's not just about our tech – it's the heart and soul of who we are. We welcome different experiences, viewpoints, and identities. For us, it’s not just the right thing to do; it’s our catalyst for sparking innovation and creativity. Our teams thrive in an environment that celebrates and supports everyone – no matter their gender, identity or expression, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion, belief, marital status, national origin, veteran status, pregnancy, or maternity status.

But we don’t just open the door to diversity – we actively welcome it. Why? Because we believe every unique voice adds something special to our team, leading us to smarter solutions and a better workplace.

So, come as you are and join our Speechling community. We’re building a place where every voice not only gets heard but is also respected and valued.

For more information on us, please visit our website and follow Speechmatics on our social channels via Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube.

We rely on legitimate interest as a legal basis for processing personal information under the GDPR for purposes of recruitment and applications for employment.
